shorts.hook: A hippo's red sweat is not blood. It's sunscreen.
shorts.title: A Hippo's Red Sweat Isn't Blood, It's Sunscreen
shorts.outro: Doug survived this one. The yawn is next. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Doug thinks the hippo is bleeding, but the red-orange "sweat" on its skin is really an oily coating that blocks UV light and slows bacteria, and the hippo is completely fine.

shorts.hook: Hippos can't gallop, but at full speed they briefly fly.
shorts.title: Hippos Can't Gallop, but at Top Speed They Briefly Fly
shorts.outro: And the hippo was only fifty meters away. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Hippos only trot, even flat out, yet the fastest ones still get all four feet off the ground for up to 15 percent of each stride, which is bad news for Doug at fifty meters.

shorts.hook: Hippos can flip a canoe from directly underneath.
shorts.title: From a Canoe, a Hippo Looks Like a Rock Until It Doesn't
shorts.outro: Then Doug stood between two bulls. The full video is linked below.
shorts.description: Hippos really do capsize boats on the Zambezi by surfacing from directly underneath, and Doug paddled right over one he thought was a rock.
